question: Which metals produce hydrogen gas when treated with very dilute nitric acid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium (Mg) and manganese (Mn)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** and **manganese (Mn)** react with very dilute nitric acid to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• When **Mg and Mn** are treated with dilute nitric acid, they displace hydrogen from the acid to form magnesium nitrate and manganese nitrate, respectively, while releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• Other metals like **copper (Cu)** and **cobalt (Co)** do not react with dilute nitric acid to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• The production of hydrogen gas depends on the reactivity series of metals where **Mg and Mn** are more reactive compared to metals like copper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• A ranking of metals based on their reactivity with water, acids, and oxygen.
 
• Highly reactive metals like potassium and sodium can react vigorously with water.
 
• Moderately reactive metals like magnesium and manganese react with acids to release hydrogen gas.
 
• Less reactive metals like copper and gold do not react with dilute acids to release hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **Nitric Acid (HNO3)**
 
 
• A strong acid commonly used in laboratories and industries.
 
• Concentrated nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent and can react violently with metals.
 
• Very dilute nitric acid, however, behaves differently and can produce hydrogen gas with some reactive metals.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2)**
 
 
• A colorless, odorless, and highly flammable gas.
 
• Produced in reactions involving acids and reactive metals.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes including hydrogenation and as a fuel in some applications.
